title: Member Handbook, Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements: Holding More Than One Agreement
content:
A member may hold more than one storage agreement at a time, and in practice most do, because an agreement covers one commodity of one crop year at one facility. This clause of the handbook sets out how many the cooperative writes, which combinations it will not write twice, and what has to be on file before grain is accepted into store under Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The test applied

1. The cooperative writes no more than six live storage agreements for one member at any moment, a ceiling of 6, counting every agreement that is not closed or terminated.

2. Two live agreements for the same member covering the same commodity, the same crop year, the same facility and the same programme are never written, because bushels would then have no single home and the free-day clock would run twice. Where a member asks for a second one the existing agreement is used instead.

3. Different programmes for the same commodity and crop year at the same facility are allowed, and that is exactly how a member keeps part of a crop on paid-up storage and the rest open.

4. The signed storage agreement and, on programmes whose entry gate calls for it, the member's stored-grain insurance certificate are on file before the agreement is accepted into store. Where they are not, the application is taken and the agreement waits in applied standing; grain arriving in the meantime is taken into open storage in the member's name rather than refused at the pit.

## Where the paperwork test is decided

The paperwork test in clause 4 is settled on the cooperative's own records of that agreement, read against the agreement number printed on the member's storage statements, and settled before the grain is accepted into store rather than after. What the member recalls signing is not the test; what the file shows against that agreement number is.

## The four particulars that make an agreement distinct

| Particular | What it records |
| --- | --- |
| Commodity | the grain the agreement holds |
| Crop year | the crop year the grain came out of |
| Facility | the licensed house holding it |
| Programme | the catalogue entry it is written under |

Two live agreements matching on all four are never written. Two live agreements matching on the first three but differing on the fourth are ordinary.

## Matters of judgement

**A member holds four live agreements and two that were closed last season. How many count against the ceiling of 6?** Four. The count takes in every agreement that is not closed or terminated, so the two closed ones fall out of it.

**A member with corn of this crop year at the Ash Grove Annex on an Open Storage Account asks for a second Open Storage Account for the same corn at the same house.** All four particulars match, so a second agreement is not written and the existing one is used.

**The same member asks instead for a Seasonal Paid-Up Storage Agreement for part of that corn at the same house.** The programme differs, so the combination is one the cooperative writes.
